finding.claim: Mass assignment: PUT /me copies the entire request body onto the authenticated user object and persists it, so any user can set privileged fields (e.g. role, isAdmin, id, email verification, tenant/org id) on their own account, leading to privilege escalation or account/tenant takeover.
finding.source: req.body (arbitrary JSON from the authenticated client)

trace.note: Object.assign merges all client-supplied keys into the server-side user object

finding.guards_checked: No allowlist, schema validation, or field filtering in this file. Authentication middleware is not visible (req.user is assumed set elsewhere), and it would not restrict which fields are writable anyway. Contrast with /me/profile at line 11, which destructures only displayName and bio and is safe. Object.assign does not invoke the __proto__ setter on the target in a way that pollutes Object.prototype, so prototype pollution is not claimed.

verdict.reason: users.js:5 runs Object.assign(req.user, req.body) with no allowlist, users.js:6 saves it, and users.js:7 echoes it back; any authenticated user can write privileged fields, and users.js is the only file in the directory, so no other guard exists.
